Elsewhere: Swiss cantons; Maximilian's Landsknechte; Spain: infantry of the Granada war.
- **Horse warfare (chariot, cavalry, horse archers)** [`cavalry_chariot`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cavalry_chariot.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. The armoured man-at-arms with his 'lance' of attendants is the core of every Italian army; Venice adds Balkan light horse (stradiots).
- **Bows of war (composite bow, crossbow, longbow)** [`crossbow_longbow`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/crossbow_longbow.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Steel crossbows are the standard missile weapon of foot and mounted troops, giving ground slowly to handguns. Elsewhere: England: longbow; Ottomans: composite bow.
- **Mechanical artillery (torsion catapult, trebuchet)** [`torsion_artillery_trebuchet`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/torsion_artillery_trebuchet.md) — K3, use none, make easy, accept low. Trebuchets have just gone out of use in favour of guns. Ancient torsion engines are known from Vitruvius and Valturio's printed De re militari.
- **Oared war galley and ram tactics** [`oared_galley_ram`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/oared_galley_ram.md) — K4, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Galleys rule Mediterranean war (boarding, a gun in the bow; no rams). Florence has let its own galleys lapse and relies on hired ships. Local: Pisa arsenal (run down); Livorno. Elsewhere: Venice Arsenal; Genoa; Naples and the Ottomans.
- **Incendiary weapons and Greek fire** [`incendiaries_greek_fire`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/incendiaries_greek_fire.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Fire pots and fire lances are used in sieges and at sea. Byzantine Greek fire is a lost legend. Elsewhere: Modena hills: natural rock oil.
- **Field fortification (marching camp, wagon fort, entrenchment)** [`field_fortification`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/field_fortification.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Ditches, fortified camps and siege trenches are familiar to Italian forces. Levied labourers help construct earthworks. Elsewhere: Bohemia, Hussite wagon forts.
- **Gunpowder (black powder)** [`gunpowder`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/gunpowder.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Made routinely; grained powder is used for handguns. Saltpetre is the bottleneck: scraped locally and imported through Venice. Local: powder makers of the commune; apothecaries.
- **Cannon and artillery** [`cannon_artillery`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cannon_artillery.md) — K4, use partial, make medium, accept high. Italian states rely on huge slow bombards throwing stone. France has lighter bronze guns with iron shot on horse-drawn wheeled carriages; Italy sees them in 1494. Local: Florentine bronze founders; artillery of the Signoria. Elsewhere: France: royal artillery; Burgundy and Germany; Ottomans.
- **Ballistics and scientific gunnery** [`ballistics_gunnery`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/ballistics_gunnery.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept high. Gunners aim by experience and guard their rules. Theory says a shot flies straight until its impetus is spent, then drops.
- **Handguns and muskets (matchlock, flintlock)** [`handguns_muskets`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/handguns_muskets.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Matchlock handguns (schioppetti, archibugi) serve in sieges and garrisons, in small companies. No wheel-lock or flintlock exists yet. Elsewhere: Milan: large handgunner companies; Brescia valleys and south Germany: gunmaking.
- **Pike and shot, volley fire and drill** [`pike_and_shot_drill`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/pike_and_shot_drill.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Handgunners fire individually from cover. Drill by word of command needs men kept under pay all year, which Florence refuses.
- **Socket bayonet** [`socket_bayonet`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/socket_bayonet.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Handguns are too few and too heavy for this to matter yet.
- **Bastioned fortification (trace italienne)** [`bastion_fortification`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/bastion_fortification.md) — K3, use partial, make hard, accept medium. Tuscany is where the transition is happening: low thick round towers, scarped walls, the first angled bastions. Full systems come after the shock of 1494. Local: Giuliano da Sangallo (Poggio Imperiale, from 1488); Sarzana citadel; Volterra fortress; Francesco di Giorgio Martini (Siena). Elsewhere: Marche: Francesco di Giorgio's fortresses (San Leo, Sassocorvaro); Ostia fortress (1480s).
- **Siegecraft, mining and counter-mining** [`siegecraft_mining`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/siegecraft_mining.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Sieges are slow: blockade, bombards, timber-propped mines. Gunpowder mines are discussed by engineers (tried by the Genoese at Sarzanello, 1487) but not mastered. Local: Francesco di Giorgio Martini (Siena).
- **Broadside gunnery and the line of battle** [`naval_gunnery_line_of_battle`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/naval_gunnery_line_of_battle.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept medium. Ships carry light guns on rails and castles to kill men before boarding. No gunports, no ship-killing guns. Elsewhere: Portugal: João II tests heavy guns low in caravels.
- **War rockets** [`war_rockets`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/war_rockets.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept low. Rockets are festival fireworks and appear in engineers' picture books; soldiers think them toys. Local: fireworks of the San Giovanni feast. Elsewhere: India and China: war rockets.
- **Standing army, pay and supply** [`standing_army_logistics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/standing_army_logistics.md) — K2, use none, make hard, accept low. - **Conscription and the mass army** [`conscription_mass_army`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/conscription_mass_army.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. Peasants of the contado are levied as pioneers and labourers only. Arming subjects is thought dangerous.

Vegetius advises clean water and moving camp; in practice siege camps rot. Camp fevers are blamed on air. Elsewhere: Castilian siege armies in the Granada war, reports of camp fever.

Engineers are hired one by one, architects doubling as fortress and siege experts; labour is levied peasants. No permanent corps.
